verdicts.flaw_description: The outcome is dated before the intervention in two cases: block One was "fitted 3 August" but gave more "by 18 June" against "the previous summer" (June precedes August inside the same summer), and block Three was "fitted 2 May" but gave more "by 17 March" against "the previous spring" (March precedes May inside the same spring). Half the cases record the yield gain before the drip line went in.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Pollen counts in each group's district ran a fifth below the previous quarter, and every group lived and slept on the district's outside air." A 20 percent fall in pollen exposure over exactly the comparison window accounts for 4-7 fewer attacks in all four groups without the inhaler doing anything.

Two cases measure the gain before the program starts: class One "started the program 6 December, scoring 8 comprehension points higher by 11 September" against "the previous autumn term" (11 September precedes 6 December within the autumn term), and class Three "started the program 20 June ... by 24 April" against "the previous spring term" (24 April precedes 20 June).

The rate is computed on a narrower population than the comparison: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout" while "about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile," so the tenth that touched the old profile is dropped from the new-profile figure while the earlier month's baseline included every board.

"Pass rates cover the students who attended every block," but "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block," so a self-selected full-attendance subset (a quarter of each cohort removed) is being compared against the whole previous spring term cohort - the 4-8 point gain can come from who was counted rather than from the tutoring.
